correctness.rationale: For greedy assignment to the larger prearrival deficit, proved by induction that every vertex with signed deficit B_v=r>0 belongs to a current tree component of size >=2^r: the newly losing endpoint has pre-deficit r-1, while the distinct receiving component has endpoint deficit >=r-1, and their union doubles the bound. Every forest component at prefix s has at most s+1 vertices, proving floor(log2(s+1)) for all prefixes. Opposite lower bound is an adaptive binary merge of two independently constructed 2^(r-1)-vertex trees whose marked vertices both have deficit r-1: the loser of one joining good receives deficit r; no cycle, and padding to exactly t edges preserves earlier prefix witness. At r=3 the construction needs 8 agents and 7 edges, and Prop1 is exactly B<=2 (eligibility-aware unit share). Independent minimax enumeration for all n<=5 and admissible t agreed, but the induction is the infinite proof.

value.rationale: A sharp, fully parameterized online fairness guarantee on the natural acyclic pair-eligibility family, with an explicit first unavoidable adaptive obstruction at 8 agents, gives a meaningful finite cutoff and universal all-n minimax theorem. It isolates the cost of irrevocability from offline or recourse-based solutions, useful for designing sequential allocations.
